transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
- Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Rylan Barton.
President Trump is in Georgia today
to try to boost Republican voter turnout,
but Republican Senate candidate Mike Collins
and gubernatorial candidate Rick Jackson
will need more than Trump's core supporters to win,
and Trump's popularity has declined in Georgia.
The rally will be the first time Jackson and Collins
have appeared at the same venue this fall.
White House press secretary Katie Zacharia
is transitioning out of her role,
according to a White House official,
not authorized to speak on the record.
It comes after President Trump suggested
that she might not stay on the job much longer.
- Katie's off to a start that the news
has been so nasty to her.
I've never seen anything like it, actually.
- Did you reconsider it?
- And I said to her, honestly, if I were you,
I'd reconsider, you'd think about it,
but I wouldn't reconsider.
- Zacharia's first official day on the job was Monday.
She came under scrutiny when she appeared uncomfortable
during her inaugural briefing,
and she was criticized for implying she'd practiced law
when she had not passed a bar exam.
The Treasury Department has closed the books
on the just-ended fiscal year,
and PR Scott Horsley reports the government ran a deficit
of almost $2 trillion.
- The government spent a lot more money
than it took in last year, $1.992 trillion more, to be exact.
That's the biggest annual deficit
since the post-pandemic year of 2021.
- Tax revenues were up 3% during the year,
but spending grew twice as fast.
Just paying interest on the federal debt last year
cost the government more than $1.3 trillion.
President Trump's double-digit tariffs
did raise some money for the government,
but the Treasury had to refund almost half
what those import taxes brought in
after the Supreme Court ruled many of the tariffs
are illegal.
It's unusual for the government's finances
to be this deep in the red when the country's not
in a recession or fighting a widespread war.
Scott Horsley, NPR News, Washington.
- Several Palestinians and an American photojournalist
for the Washington Post were beaten and injured
by settlers in the Israeli-occupied West Bank today.
The Washington Post said the attack happened
when Palestinians were trying to gather their olive harvest,
and Piers Hadil Al-Shalchi reports violence
against Palestinians and journalists in the West Bank
has risen recently.
- The Washington Post said that the Israeli settlers
set Palestinian olive groves on fire
and hurled stones using slingshots.
It said that veteran photojournalist Heidi Levine
was wearing a protective vest clearly marked
with the word "press."
In an Instagram post, Levine said a group of settlers
knocked her to the ground.
- They just kept kicking me and kicking me
probably 50 times.
- The paper said she was receiving medical care
and was safe.
In a statement, the Washington Post called
for a "thorough investigation."
The Israeli police condemned the attacks
and said it would investigate.
Witnesses said Israeli soldiers
did not stop the settler assaults.
Hadil Al-Shalchi, NPR News.
Stocks closed lower on Wall Street today
as more drops for big tech companies
weighed down the market.
The S&P 500 lost more than 1%.
The NASDAQ sank more than 2%.
This is NPR News.
The NCAA has filed a federal lawsuit
against Ohio Republican Governor Mike DeWine.
This comes after DeWine signed an executive order
allowing Ohio colleges to let athletes who graduated
in 2022 play a fifth year.
The NCAA president says the lawsuit
aims to prevent DeWine from disrupting
fair competition among schools.
The order allows public and private universities
in Ohio to let athletes play despite the NCAA's new rule,
excluding those who have played four seasons.
Tesla has unveiled a new sports car.
The EV uses built-in thrusters to leap over obstacles
and it can go from zero to 60 in under one second.
NPR's John Ruich reports.
- The Tesla Roadster is a collaboration
between Tesla and SpaceX and CEO Elon Musk
unveiled it at a SpaceX rocket test center in Texas.
It has 10 built-in nozzles that use ultra high pressure air
that can propel the car down the road
or make it jump into the air and do a barrel roll.
It also has fans that can push it down toward the road
for better traction.
Tesla has been investing in self-driving technology
and Musk said the Roadster would eventually be
the only manually driven car in the lineup.
The angular sports car, he said,
is better than any James Bond car
and will enter production in 2028.
He added though that it's not necessarily safety optimized
and might not be legal.
John Ruich, NPR News.
- Leaf peeping season is underway.
According to the foliage report website,
New England is having an elite year
thanks to adequate spring and summer rain
plus warm days and cool nights heading into fall.
Colorado, meanwhile, is having a lackluster foliage season
because of extreme droughts.
I'm Rylan Barton, this is NPR News.
- This message comes from Kachava.
Sometimes flavors need a pinch of salt
to unleash their full potential, kind of like life.
A little saltiness can keep things interesting
and deliciously sweet.
Fuel your salty sweet cravings with Kachava's
new salted caramel all in one nutrition shake.
Just two scoops provide protein, fiber, greens, and more.
Embrace your salty side.
Go to kachava.com and use code NPR
for 15% off your first order.
That's K-A-C-H-A-V-A.com, code NPR.

topics.text: President Trump rallies in Georgia to boost turnout for Collins and Jackson
White House press secretary Katie Zacharia transitioning out of her role after days on job
US government posts nearly $2 trillion annual deficit, largest since 2021, Treasury reports
Israeli settlers attack Palestinians and Washington Post photojournalist Heidi Levine in West Bank
Stocks close lower on Wall Street as big tech companies drag the market down
NCAA files federal lawsuit against Ohio Governor Mike DeWine over fifth-year athlete order
Tesla unveils Roadster sports car with built-in thrusters, built with SpaceX, production in 2028
New England has elite fall foliage season while Colorado's is lackluster due to drought
